summary: Cabo Rojo Light marks Puerto Rico's southwest corner: built by the Spanish in 1878-1882, automated in 1967, opened to visitors in 2007.

lens.where: Nomination says the lantern 'still houses' the 1881 lens when written; LighthouseFriends says the lantern 'originally housed' a third-order lens; the archive gives the current optic as DCB-24. Present lens not established.

structures.note: 18.30 m including the lantern (1981 nomination); 40 ft (12.2 m) from its base in the 1901 report
One storey (1901 report); designed for 1st and 3rd class keepers (1981 nomination); stone (archive); interior altered 1959

access.note: Coast Guard property managed by the Municipality of Cabo Rojo; open to visitors since March 2007 (LighthouseFriends). The archive record still says not open to the public.

visit.note: Staircase to the roof open to visitors (LighthouseFriends)

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner); Municipio de Cabo Rojo (manager)

events.note: Tower begun by the Spanish (1901 report: commenced in 1878)
Original lenticular Sautter, Lemonnier & Cie. lens dated 1881 by the 1981 nomination; the 1901 report gives the tower's completion as 1882
Tower finished by the Spanish at a cost of 14,900 pesos
Current tower first lit 1882 (Coast Guard list); the archive gives 1868 for station establishment, unexplained in the sources read
Hurricane passed just off the south coast of Puerto Rico, 11 August 1915
Keeper Jose Escalera Velez and assistant rescued three men from a small boat about a mile from the station
September 1921 hurricane over Puerto Rico; Cape Rojo among the ninth-district lights damaged; group figures only (four boats lost, many buildings damaged)
Storm on the evening of 23 July damaged lighthouse property at Cape Rojo; principal damage at Mona Island
Interior altered: bathrooms, kitchens and bedrooms reconfigured
Weight-driven clock replaced by an electric motor
Light automated; lighthouse left unmanned and boarded up
Characteristics changed; in 1981 the fixed white light had a 15-mile range and the flashing 22 miles
National Register of Historic Places; the nomination's date-entered stamp reads October 22, 1981 (OCR)
Opened to the public in March 2007

corrections.why: The archive's place record says 'Open to Public: No'. LighthouseFriends reports the lighthouse open to visitors since March 2007, managed by the Municipality of Cabo Rojo. The archive line may be out of date; check before changing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive record gives 1868 for the station's establishment and its original lens; the Coast Guard list gives 1882 for the first lighting of the current tower, and the 1901 report dates the tower's building to 1878-1882. No source read describes an earlier light at this point, so the story dates the present light from 1882 and leaves the 1868 date unexplained.

Not resolved. The 1901 report gives 40 feet from the base, and the archive gives 40 feet from base to the centre of the lantern; the 1981 nomination gives 18.30 m (60 ft) including the lantern. The story states the disagreement and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: (1) Keepers: the archive's roster, printed by roster.py (USLHS place 3473, showPeople/3473), 38 lines, matched by name and position (0.38 km). Keeper names and spans are the archive's; none was checked against a primary NARA register for this story. 'At least' marks a documented span. (2) Arturo Machicote Ferrer (page image of the 1915 Bulletin, PDF page 35, printed p. 180, checked 2026-10-22: 'Arturo Machicote Ferrer, assistant keeper, of Cape Rojo Light Station'; the OCR text reads 'Ferrel'' and is kept as the evidence quote), LighthouseFriends (Arturo Machicote Ferrer), archive (Arturo M. Ferrer, first assistant from at least 1915). The name match is not connected by any source to the 1915 rescue; the story does not treat the archive entry as the same man. (3) Cross-station names: the archive lists Felix R. Giraldet at Cabo Rojo (at least 1911 to at least 1913) and at Cardona Island (at least 1917 to at least 1921), and Simeon Martin at both (1901-1902 here); the archive shares a person slug in each case. Not confirmed as the same man in a primary record; not used in this story. (4) Dates: the archive record gives 1868 for station establishment and original lens; the Coast Guard list gives 1882 for the current tower's first lighting; the 1981 nomination dates its lens to 1881. The 1868 date is not explained by any source read. (5) Height: 40 ft from the base (1901 report), 40 ft base to lantern centre (archive), 18.30 m including the lantern (nomination). Stated as a disagreement. (6) Range: the record says 11 nautical miles; the 1901 report says visible 18 miles, and the 1981 nomination gives 15 miles fixed and 22 flashing. The record figure is not used. (7) Characteristic: the record's Fl W 20s is not confirmed in any source read; the story does not use it. (8) OCR and images: the 1915 Bulletin OCR garbles names ('Escalern', 'Ferrel''); the page image (checked) reads 'Jose Escalera Velez, keeper' and 'Arturo Machicote Ferrer, assistant keeper'. The 1926 Bulletin page 33 image reads 'The tropical hurricane of July 22-29, 1926' and 'Ponce Range' (OCR: 'Pence Range'); the story says 'a storm' and 'Ponce Range' from the image. The 1921 Bulletin PDF page 37 image reads 'On September 9 and 10, 1921' and 'Four boats were lost' (OCR: 'Fom'); the story uses the month only. (9) Printed page: the 1901 report entry is at scan page 107; the index gives printed page 79 for Cape Rojo. (10) NRHP listing date (22 October 1981) comes from the nomination's date-entered stamp, read from OCR as 'OCT221981' (the same date as the Cardona NPGallery date-published record, which is an asset date). The story says 'when the nomination was written' rather than a year, since the nomination's own stamp reads 'RECEIVED 1980'. (11) Opening hours and visiting information are LighthouseFriends' (undated); check before any visit. The archive record still reads 'Open to Public: No'; LighthouseFriends says 'Grounds/tower open'. (12) Coast Guard list gives 'Automated? YES 1967'. The nomination says 1967 too. (13) No photos proposed. (14) Fact-check 2026-10-22: quotes re-checked (49 found on the first run); story sentences checked against the NRHP pages, USLHS place record, LighthouseFriends, USCG list, the 1901 report scan page 107, the 1915, 1921 and 1926 Bulletins (page images), and the archive roster as printed by roster.py.
